text.tspan: Period: 2020–2024 Coverage: 8 Major U.S. Metro Markets Date: December 20, 2024

text.id: U.S. residential real estate prices have risen sharply across all major metros between 2020 and 2024, driven by pandemic-era migration, persistently low housing inventory, and the long-term impact of remote work on buyer preferences. Austin recorded the steepest appreciation at +66%, while traditionally expensive markets like New York (+24%) and Los Angeles (+21%) saw more moderate gains. Mortgage rates above 7% have dampened transaction volumes significantly, but prices have remained resilient due to supply constraints. First-time buyer affordability has deteriorated to its worst level in over 30 years.
